note: Literature consistently highlights the absence of ectopia lentis as a hallmark distinguishing Loeys-Dietz syndrome subtypes (including SMAD2/LDS6) from Marfan syndrome.

evidence.text: Absence of ectopia lentis alongside features such as cleft palate, bifid uvula, and hypertelorism is a key clinical criterion that suggests Loeys-Dietz syndrome (including SMAD2-related disease) rather than Marfan syndrome.

source.title: Marfan syndrome and related disorders
source.quote: Features such as cleft palate, bifid uvula, hypertelorism, craniosynostosis and osteoarthritis and the absence of ectopia lentis suggest Loeys Dietz.

evidence.text: Absence of ectopia lentis is recognized as a major distinguishing feature of Loeys-Dietz syndrome, although few SMAD2 mutation-positive cases had initially been characterized.
